body.p: The Office Action of February 15, 2024, has been considered. By way of this response, claims 1, 3, 5, 10-11, 18, and 20 have been amended, claims 2, 4, and 12-13 have been cancelled without prejudice to their further prosecution, and claims 22-28 have been added. No new matter has been added. All claims are fully supported by the original disclosure. Favorable reconsideration and allowance of this application are respectfully requested.

The Applicant thanks Examiner Acosta and Examiner McFall for the courtesies extended to Marianne Buckley (Registration No. 68,104) and Michael Van Ryn (Registration No. 81,871)of Hanley, Flight and Zimmerman, LLC, during the telephonic interview conducted on April 8, 2024. During the interview, the parties discussed amendments to claim 1 substantially as presented herewith, in view of the 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejections in the present Office Action. Examiner Acosta agreed that the amendments to claim 1 overcome the rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 103.

The Applicant also thanks Examiner Acosta for the courtesies extended during a telephone interview conducted on May 13, 2024, with Michael Van Ryn (Registration No.81,871). During the interview, the parties discussed the Applicant's after-final response filed on April 11, 2024. No agreement was reached.
Claims 1, 7-10, 11, 15-16, 18-19, and 21 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as

allegedly unpatentable over Landers et al. (EP 3907136), hereinafter "Landers," in view of Moon et al. (KR 102004227), hereinafter "Moon." Claims 2-5, 12-13, and 20 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Landers in view of Moon and Rambo (US Patent Application Publication No. 2022/0243667). Claim 14 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Landers in view of Moon and Lavoie et al. (EP 3578464), hereinafter Lavoie. Claim 17 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Landers in view of Moon and Mariotto (EP 3805107). The Applicant respectfully traverses all of the reference-based rejections.

Nonetheless, at the above-referenced Examiner interview of April 8, 2024, Examiner Acosta indicated that claim 1 substantially as presented herein overcomes the cited references. Similar amendments have been made to independent claims 11 and 18. Thus, claims 1, 11, and 18, and their respective dependent claims are in condition for allowance. Withdrawal of the § 103 rejections of claims 1, 11, 18, and all claims depending therefrom is respectfully requested.

In general, the Office Action makes various statements regarding the claims. Thus, the Applicant will not address such statements at the present time. However, the Applicant expressly reserves the right to challenge such statements in the future should the need arise (e.g., if such statements should become relevant by appearing in a rej ection of any current or future claim).
The Commissioner is hereby authorized to refund any overpayment and charge any

deficiency in the amount paid in connection with this paper (if any) or any additional fees which may be required during the pendency of this application under 37 C.F.R. § 1.16 or § 1.17 to Deposit Account No. 50-2455.

In addition, if a petition for an extension of time under 37 C.F.R. § 1.136(a) is necessary to maintain the pendency of this case and is not otherwise requested in this case, the Applicant requests that the Commissioner consider this paper to be a petition for an extension of time and authorizes the Commissioner to charge the fee as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 1.17(a) corresponding to the needed extension of time to Deposit Account No. 50-2455.
